findings.title: A failed onboarding leaves a half-initialised Vault: myelin.yaml, the scaffold and an empty .git stay, the personal pack that myelin.yaml lists is deleted, and the retry is refused with 409
findings.story: A new user points the Hub at a folder that already has notes — an existing Obsidian vault — and defines their own Domain in the wizard. The Hub writes packs/me.my-domains, runs init_vault (myelin.yaml + scaffold), writes the welcome draft, runs git init and stages everything with `git add -A`. The Vault pre-commit device rejects the first commit because an old note has no frontmatter → 500. The error handler then removes only the personal pack ('no half-initialised directory left behind'). Result: myelin.yaml lists me.my-domains and the Domain it declared, the pack is gone, there is no commit, and clicking the wizard again answers 409 'Vault already initialised'. The first 15 minutes of exactly the people MYELIN is meant to spread to.

fix.summary: onboard() captures the folder's state before its first write (_OnboardUndo: existing directories, whether .git/.myelin existed, bytes of .gitignore and of an existing personal pack). On any failure it removes the files of the scaffold plan and the welcome draft, restores the two files it may have overwritten, drops the Vault/index, removes the .myelin and .git it created and every directory that did not exist before and is empty now. The user's own files are not touched; the error names the cause; the same request succeeds once the cause is fixed.
